edges.description: Reduced EF-Tu activity limits delivery of charged aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitochondrial ribosome, which is the elongation step itself.

The thirteen mtDNA-encoded subunits are distributed across complexes I, III, IV and V, so under-supplying all of them makes those four complexes fail together while complex II, built entirely from nuclear-encoded subunits, is spared.
Glycolytic compensation converts the accumulating pyruvate to lactate, which leaves the cell.
The developing brain has a high and inflexible oxidative demand, which is why it is the organ most consistently and most severely affected.

Cardiac muscle is likewise oxidative-dependent. The step itself is as direct as the encephalopathy branch; what is unexplained is why it dominates in some patients and is absent in others, which is recorded as an open question rather than as missing intermediate steps.
The clinical and laboratory manifestation of the accumulated lactate.
The clinical manifestation by which this node is recognised.
A malformation of cortical development, so this edge asserts the energy deficit acts during brain formation rather than only degrading a formed brain.
The destructive white-matter component, reported as macrocystic leukodystrophy in the index patient.
The alternative cardiac morphology, reported in the adult patient.
The mutant shows compromised mitochondrial protein translation, which is the step EF-Tu performs, measured directly rather than inferred.
edges.limitations: A full knockout rather than a knock-in of a patient missense allele, so it models complete loss of EF-Tu while every reported human genotype is missense with residual activity. That difference matters for this disease specifically, because allele severity is the candidate explanation for the organ selectivity seen in patients. Zebrafish larvae also differ from human infants in oxygen delivery and in reliance on glycolysis.

edges.description: The mutant shows dysfunctional mitochondria with oxidative phosphorylation defects, the cellular consequence this node records.
edges.limitations: The source reports an oxidative phosphorylation defect without a complex-by-complex breakdown, so the model does not resolve whether complex II is spared - which is the open question on the human node.

edges.description: The same study screened for interventions and put forward probucol as a candidate for managing COXPD4. This is the only therapeutic lead reported for the disease, and it is entirely preclinical.
edges.limitations: The abstract states probucol is a promising approach without reporting which readout it corrected or by how much, so the rescue is recorded as a claim made by the source rather than a quantified effect, and no readout is attached. It is also a rescue in a full knockout, while every reported human genotype is missense with residual EF-Tu - so even a real effect here would not straightforwardly predict benefit in patients. Fidelity is LOW for that reason, and nothing about this link should be read as clinical evidence.

nodes.description: Biallelic missense variants in TUFM reduce the function of mitochondrial elongation factor Tu. EF-Tu is a GTPase whose job is to bind charged aminoacyl-tRNAs and escort them to the mitochondrial ribosome, so a hypomorphic EF-Tu limits the rate at which the ribosome can be supplied with substrate. The pathogenicity of the alleles was established experimentally by functional complementation rather than inferred from conservation alone.

nodes.description: Cardiac involvement has been the presenting and dominant problem in two patients, and it took a different form in each: a dilated cardiomyopathy in an infant with lactic acidosis but no progressive encephalopathy, and a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the only reported adult. TUFM therefore belongs in the differential for metabolic cardiomyopathy of either morphology, and these two cases are the clearest evidence that the disease is not obligately neurological. Nothing explains why the morphology differs.

nodes.description: With four of the five respiratory complexes under-assembled, cells cannot meet their ATP demand by oxidative phosphorylation and fall back on glycolysis. Tissues differ in how much slack they have, which is why the organs that fail are the ones with the highest and least flexible oxidative demand.

nodes.description: Complexes I, III, IV and V each contain at least one mtDNA-encoded subunit and cannot be assembled in normal amounts when mitochondrial translation is limiting. Complex II contains none and is spared. That pattern - several complexes down together with complex II normal - is the diagnostic signature that distinguishes a translation defect from a lesion in an individual complex, and it is what the "combined" in the disease name denotes.

nodes.description: Mitochondria run a translation apparatus of their own, separate from the cytosolic one, dedicated to the thirteen proteins encoded by mitochondrial DNA. EF-Tu is a shared component of that apparatus, not a subunit-specific factor, so limiting it throttles synthesis of all thirteen products simultaneously rather than any one of them selectively.

nodes.description: The dominant clinical picture in the classical presentation: rapidly progressive, frequently fatal encephalopathy from the neonatal or early infantile period, with microcephaly. Neuroimaging in the index EF-Tu patient showed severe infantile macrocystic leukodystrophy with micropolygyria, and MONDO's description of the disease likewise records polymicrogyria with white-matter abnormality - a malformation of cortical development alongside the destructive white-matter change, indicating that the energy deficit acts during brain formation and not only after it.

meta.association: TUFM encodes mitochondrial elongation factor Tu, a GTPase that binds charged aminoacyl-tRNAs and delivers them to the A site of the mitochondrial ribosome. It is one of three nuclear-encoded elongation factors of the mitochondrial translation apparatus, alongside TSFM (EF-Ts) and GFM1 (EF-G1); pathogenic variants in each cause a combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency, and the three were among the first nuclear-gene causes of a mitochondrial translation defect to be identified. Reported TUFM alleles are missense, so residual elongation capacity is retained.

nodes.description: A zebrafish tufm knockout generated specifically as a COXPD4 model. It reproduces the proximal half of the human mechanism directly - impaired mitochondrial protein translation and consequent oxidative phosphorylation defects - and adds a metabolic readout, suppression of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, that has not been measured in patients.
